newsitem.title: USA: Miami cruise ship passengers sickened by virus.
newsitem.headline: Miami cruise ship passengers sickened by virus.

text.p: A common gastrointestinal virus was responsible for an illness that swept a Miami-based cruise ship on a Caribbean voyage this week, a health official said on Saturday.

The virus, similar to the common "Norwalk" virus, sickened more than 350 passengers and crew aboard the Norwegian Caribbean Cruise Line vessel Royal Odyssey during a 10-day cruise, said Dave Forney, a public health adviser with the U.S. Centres for Disease Control.
It was the third consecutive cruise that some passengers aboard the Royal Odyssey had been stricken by the virus, which was identified in patients' stool samples, Forney said.
The cruise line agreed to cancel a voyage scheduled for next week following a recommendation from health authorities, Forney said.

"We recommended not to sail. That doesn't confine them to port. It's not a quarantine situation," he said, adding that health officials could have ordered the ship to remain in port had the cruise line not agreed with the recommendation.
The Royal Odyssey was scheduled for refurbishing and would be in port at least 30 days, during which time the cruise line would take measures to eliminate the virus, he said.
Officials said 306 of the 781 passengers and 50 of 379 crew experienced vomiting and diarrhoea during the cruise. The ship left Miami on March 25 and docked at the Port of Miami on Friday.

The Miami Herald reported that the ship's route included Tortola and St. John's in the Virgin Islands, St. Barts, St. Kitts, San Juan, Puerto Rico and Great Stirrup Cay, the cruise line's private island in the Bahamas.
A spokeswoman for the company told the Herald that the ailing passengers were treated with an over-the-counter medication.
Forney said during a cruise several weeks ago, nearly half the passengers on board had reported symptoms of the virus.
